page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v7 is an Esv7-family virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance has no local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong capabilities in memory-intensive and cryptographic operations. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 68,865.84 and a database operations score of 22,699.83, both placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks reached 3,690.93 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths returned to average levels at 175.88 GB/sec and 69.26 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression performed in the top 10% at 36.68 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 321.51 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the system processed small-model (135M) text generation at a top-tier rate of 353.0 tokens/sec, while medium-model (7B) text generation operated at 27.93 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48s_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external Premium Storage, which represents a structural tradeoff for I/O-heavy tasks. Given its strong database operations, high Redis SET performance of 83.33 million operations per second, and robust memory bandwidth, this server is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application hosting, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
